title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
gist: Google launched Tool Retrieval (preview) in the Gemini Interactions API: agents hold large tool libraries with only names/descriptions in context and load parameter schemas on demand via a server-side tool_search, cutting input tokens and latency and preserving tool-selection accuracy as libraries grow. It has no separate charge, works with remote MCP servers and prefix caching, supports client-side retrieval, and runs on Gemini 3.6+ including all Gemini 4 models.

themes.theme: Tool bloat as an agent scaling bottleneck

insights.claim: Sending every full tool parameter schema on every request to an agent with dozens or hundreds of tools inflates input tokens, adds latency, and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the candidate list grows, according to Google's Gemini API team.
insights.speaker: Lucia Loher
insights.so_what: Context cost and accuracy degradation from large tool sets are a real constraint on agent scale; vendors solving it gain stickiness with enterprise agent builders.
insights.quote: It inflates input token counts, adds latency, and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the candidate list grows.
insights.locator: When an agent connects to dozens or even hundreds of tools

insights.claim: Google launched Tool Retrieval in preview in the Gemini Interactions API, letting agents keep a full tool library on standby and load parameter schemas only when the current task needs them.
insights.speaker: Lucia Loher
insights.so_what: Signals the Interactions API is Google's strategic surface for agent features; new agentic capabilities are landing there first.

insights.claim: Gemini Tool Retrieval works by adding a tool_search tool and setting defer_loading: true on tools; the model still sees every deferred tool's name and description, requests a tool by name, and the API loads its schema and the model emits the function call all within a single request.
insights.speaker: Lucia Loher
insights.so_what: Single-call search+load+call avoids extra round trips, making the approach cheap to adopt for developers already on Gemini function calling.
insights.quote: When the model needs a tool, it asks for it by name, the API loads the full schema, and the model calls the function, all inside the same request.

insights.claim: Gemini's server-side Tool Retrieval requires no developer-built or hosted index: Gemini runs the search on the server, and developers can keep most-used tools loaded up front while deferring the long tail.
insights.speaker: Lucia Loher
insights.so_what: Removing retrieval infrastructure from the developer lowers switching friction and competes with DIY tool-RAG stacks and middleware vendors.
insights.quote: There's no index to build or host.
insights.locator: From here it's normal function calling

insights.claim: Gemini Tool Retrieval preserves prefix caching because deferred schemas stay out of the start of the prompt and loaded schemas are appended later in the conversation, keeping the cached prefix stable across turns.
insights.speaker: Lucia Loher
insights.so_what: Compatibility with caching compounds the token savings, improving unit economics for long multi-turn agent sessions on Gemini.
insights.locator: Tool Retrieval also plays well with prefix caching

insights.claim: Setting defer_loading: true on a remote mcp_server tool in the Gemini API loads every tool that MCP server exposes on demand, so large MCP servers can be connected without listing their tools individually.
insights.speaker: Lucia Loher
insights.so_what: Deepening MCP support shows Google embracing the cross-vendor tool protocol, making large MCP integrations more practical on Gemini.
insights.locator: Tool Retrieval also works with remote MCP servers

insights.claim: Gemini also supports client-side tool retrieval (tool_search with "execution": "client") for developers with their own tool registry, embedding index, or per-user permission filter, at the cost of one extra round trip per search, and it allows exposing new tools mid-conversation.
insights.speaker: Lucia Loher
insights.so_what: Enterprises with permissioned tool registries can keep control of retrieval, widening the addressable set of enterprise agent deployments.
insights.quote: Client-side retrieval adds one round trip per search, because your app runs the lookup.

insights.claim: Gemini Tool Retrieval has no separate charge: enabling tool_search adds a small fixed block of input tokens, and each loaded schema is billed as input for the rest of the conversation, so savings occur only when unloaded schemas outweigh loaded ones, which Google says is the usual case for large libraries.
insights.speaker: Lucia Loher
insights.so_what: Savings are workload-dependent; Google itself tells developers to measure against their own traffic, so token-revenue impact is ambiguous.
insights.quote: You save tokens when the schemas you never load outweigh the ones you do, which is the usual case for large libraries.
insights.locator: How pricing and supported models work

insights.claim: Tool Retrieval works with Gemini 3.6 and later models, including all Gemini 4 models, in the Interactions API.
insights.speaker: Lucia Loher
insights.so_what: Feature gating to newer models nudges developers to migrate onto Gemini 4-era models.
insights.quote: Tool Retrieval works with Gemini 3.6 and later models, including all Gemini 4 models, in the Interactions API.
